title: 22. Interview: Hybrid Search
summary: Interview Q&A for Hybrid Search — 7 questions with model answers.
objectives: Answer 7 Hybrid Search interview questions out loud
Lead with the concept, then a small example, then a tradeoff

sections.title: Step 11 — Interview Preparation
sections.body:
### A. Conceptual Interview Questions

**Q1: What is the fundamental difference between sparse and dense retrieval?**
> **Answer:** Sparse retrieval (BM25) represents documents as high-dimensional sparse vectors — only the words that appear get non-zero values. The vocabulary might be 500K terms but each document has values for only ~200-1000 of them. Dense retrieval represents any document as a fixed-size dense vector (e.g., 768 or 1536 dimensions) where ALL dimensions are non-zero. Sparse is exact (keyword match), dense is approximate (semantic meaning). The tradeoff: sparse is interpretable and exact, dense is semantically aware but opaque.

**Q2: Why is RRF better than linear score combination for hybrid search?**
> **Answer:** Linear score combination (0.5 * bm25_score + 0.5 * vector_score) fails because the scores are on different scales. BM25 scores can range from 0 to 30+, while cosine similarity is typically 0.7-1.0 for top results. You'd need careful normalization. RRF solves this elegantly: it's rank-based, not score-based. Rank 1 always gets 1/(k+1) regardless of whether it came from BM25 or vector. No normalization needed. Additionally, RRF is theoretically grounded (similar to Condorcet voting) and robust to outliers.

**Q3: Explain the difference between bi-encoder and cross-encoder. When do you use each?**
> **Answer:** Bi-encoder encodes query and document SEPARATELY → produces independent vectors → similarity via dot product or cosine. Fast because document vectors are pre-computed. Used for first-stage retrieval (millions of candidates). Cross-encoder takes (query, document) as a PAIR → processes them together with full attention → outputs a single relevance score. Much more accurate (sees interaction between query and doc tokens) but must run at query time and can't be pre-computed. Used for reranking top-50-200 candidates from first stage. Rule: bi-encoder for scale, cross-encoder for quality.

**Q4: How would you handle a query that needs both exact matching and semantic understanding?**
> **Answer:** This is exactly what hybrid search is designed for. Example: "GPT-4 hallucination mitigation techniques". "GPT-4" needs exact match (BM25 critical — vector might return "LLM" generically). "hallucination mitigation" needs semantic understanding (vectors find "reducing factual errors", "groundedness", "RAG approaches" which BM25 misses). Solution: Run both, fuse with RRF. Optionally, apply query analysis: detect that "GPT-4" is a named entity → boost BM25 weight specifically for that term in the query.

**Q5: What happens to hybrid search performance when the embedding model goes out of distribution?**
> **Answer:** Dense retrieval quality collapses. If the domain has terminology the embedding model never saw in training (e.g., medical jargon, new product names), embeddings won't capture semantic similarity correctly. "CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing" might embed close to "gene" but miss the specific technique. This is where hybrid search shines: BM25 still catches exact term matches via IDF, providing a graceful fallback. Hybrid system degrades to "mostly BM25" rather than failing completely. Detection: monitor bi-encoder's top-1 relevance score distribution — if mean drops, model may be out of distribution.

### B. Scenario-Based Questions

**Scenario 1: nDCG@10 drops from 0.73 to 0.61 after upgrading embedding model**

> **Root Cause Investigation:**
> 1. New model has different embedding space — old vectors incompatible
> 2. Did re-indexing happen? → If not, query vectors and document vectors from different spaces → garbage results
> 3. Is new model better on general benchmarks but worse on your specific domain?
>
> **Investigation:**
> - Check: was the vector index rebuilt with new model?
> - Segment degradation by query type: general queries vs. domain-specific
> - Run ablation: disable vector, use BM25-only → if nDCG improves → vector is the problem
>
> **Fix:**
> - Re-index ALL documents with new model before switching
> - A/B test: old model vs new model on 10% traffic before full rollout
> - Consider fine-tuning new model on your domain data

**Scenario 2: Search latency degrades from 100ms to 800ms under Black Friday load**

> **Root Cause Analysis:**
> - Cross-encoder reranker CPU/GPU saturated
> - Vector search index under memory pressure (evictions)
> - BM25 shard query queue backing up
>
> **Quick mitigations:**
> 1. Reduce reranker candidates from 100 → 20 under high load (load-sensitive)
> 2. Short-circuit: if cache hit rate > 70% → most load absorbed by cache
> 3. Add circuit breaker: skip reranker if latency > 150ms, return RRF results
> 4. Pre-compute results for top-1000 expected queries (holiday-specific)
>
> **Architecture fix:**
> - Add dedicated GPU cluster for reranker
> - Implement adaptive quality: high load → use faster model (MiniLM-L-2 vs L-12)
> - Horizontal scaling: add more BM25 shards, more vector replicas

### C. System Design Question

**Design: Enterprise Knowledge Search for 50M internal documents, 10K concurrent users**

```
Architecture:

INGESTION PIPELINE:
  Documents → Parser (Apache Tika)
           → Chunker (512 tokens, 64 overlap)
           → [BM25 branch] → Elasticsearch (10 shards, 2 replicas)
           → [Vector branch] → Embedding service (GPU cluster)
                            → Qdrant vector DB (distributed, 8 nodes)
           
QUERY PIPELINE:
  User → Query API (FastAPI, 20 instances behind load balancer)
       → Cache check (Redis Cluster, 1TB, TTL=15min)
       → Parallel:
           BM25 (Elasticsearch, <10ms p99)
           Vector (Qdrant HNSW, <30ms p99)
       → RRF Fusion (in-memory, 1ms)
       → Cross-encoder (16 GPU instances, max 100 candidates, 80ms p99)
       → Business logic (access control, freshness, personalization)
       → Return top-10

ACCESS CONTROL (critical for enterprise):
  - Documents tagged with ACL (access control lists)
  - Elasticsearch: field-level security filters on every query
  - Vector DB: namespace isolation per user group
  - Never show documents user lacks permission to see

SCALE MATH:
  10K concurrent users × 2 QPS = 20K QPS
  Cache hit rate 40%: → 12K QPS to backend
  BM25: 12K QPS / 10 shards = 1200 QPS per shard (manageable)
  Vector: 12K QPS / 8 nodes = 1500 QPS per node (needs GPU)
  Reranker: 12K × 0ms (cache hits absorbed) → manageable
```
